summary: Charles Edmund Godakumbura was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Kingswood College and served as Senior Lecturer at the University of London circa 1953–1960.
Charles Elliott worked in Indology. He served at the East India Company circa 1795–1826 and was Treasurer of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland circa 1837–1856.

Charles Gabriel Seligman studied at St Thomas' Hospital (circa 1892–1896) and worked in Indology and other fields. He taught Bronislaw Malinowski and held a post at the University of London circa 1910–1934.

Charles Goodman is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan in 2002 under Allan Gibbard and was an Associate Professor at Binghamton University (attested 2013).

Charles H. Long, a religious studies scholar, studied at the University of Chicago (circa 1949–1962). He held posts at UNC Chapel Hill (circa 1974–1987), Syracuse University (circa 1987–1991), UC Santa Barbara, and Chicago.

Charles Hallisey studied at Colgate, Harvard, UPenn, and the University of Chicago. A religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar, he taught at Loyola University Chicago (circa 1988–1996), Harvard University, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

Charles Henry Tawney studied at Trinity College, Cambridge. An Indologist, he was Principal of Presidency University, Kolkata (1876–1892) and Librarian at the India Office and India Office Library (1892/1893–1903).

Charles Malamoud, a scholar of Indology and religious studies, studied at the University of Paris (circa 1948–1954). He held posts at the University of Lyon (circa 1968–1979) and École Pratique des Hautes Études (circa 1979–1999).

Charles Philip Brown studied at Haileybury and Imperial Service College (circa 1814–1817). A scholar of Indology and linguistics, he served in the Indian Civil Service (circa 1817–1854) and as Professor of Telugu at the University of London (circa 1855–1869).

Charles Ramble studied at Durham University and under Michael Aris. A scholar of Tibetology and religious studies, he held posts at Wolfson College, Oxford (circa 2000–2010), the University of Oxford, and École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Charles Rieu studied at Geneva and Bonn, learning under Jean Humbert, Christian Lassen, G. W. Freytag, and Johannes Gildemeister. Working in Indology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and linguistics, he held posts at the British Museum and Cambridge.

Indologist and linguist Charles Rockwell Lanman studied at Yale, and under William Dwight Whitney and Rudolf von Roth. He taught at Johns Hopkins (circa 1876–1880) and served as Professor at Harvard University from 1880.

Charles S. Prebish studied at Case Western Reserve University and under David M. Miller and Richard Hugh Robinson. A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, he served as Professor at Pennsylvania State University (circa 1973–2007).

Charles Wei-hsun Fu was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at National Taiwan University and the University of Illinois System, and held a post at Ohio University circa 1969–1972.

Charles Wilkins was an Indologist and a founding member of the Asiatic Society. He served as Oriental Librarian for the East India Company and as Librarian for the India Office Library and Records circa 1801–1836.

Charles de Harlez worked in sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He served as Professor and Professor of Oriental Languages at KU Leuven circa 1871–1899, where he taught Louis de La Vallée Poussin.
Chatral Sangye Dorje Rinpoche was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sera Khandro and Dorje Dradul, and taught Keith Dowman and Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche.

Chatsumarn Kabilsingh studied at Visva-Bharati, McMaster, and Magadh universities. A Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who founded the Sakyadhita International Association of Buddhist Women, she served as Professor of Philosophy at Thammasat University circa 1973–2000.

Chen-kuo Lin studied Buddhist philosophy at Temple University. A scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, he served as Professor and Distinguished Professor at National Chengchi University and held visiting posts at IIAS and Leiden University.
Cheng Yen is an active figure in Buddhist and religious studies who studied as a disciple under Yin Shun circa 1963–2005 and founded Tzu Chi.
